title: AMD Stock Is Entering a New Cycle‼️Listen Up

keyPoints.text: AMD reportedly plans roughly a 10% price increase starting in Q4 across accelerators, consumer GPUs, and motherboard chipsets due to rising TSMC wafer costs, which could mathematically result in net margin expansion for AMD.
If crude oil peaks in the next month or two, 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields are likely to peak as well, setting up rate-sensitive equities for strong upside rallies.

Waiting for growth metrics to look great or for a company to reach full profitability often causes investors to miss massive multi-bagger upside, as illustrated by historical moves in Palantir and Tesla.

A guest commentator argues the Fed should have implemented a 50 basis point hike as a 'stun and done' move because inflation numbers are not decreasing quickly enough, while the host notes a 75 basis point hike would have driven Treasury yields down aggressively.
The commentator highlights that unadjusted import and export price averages sit at 7.8%, reflecting stubborn underlying inflation without artificial quality or seasonal adjustments.

A more aggressive 75 basis point rate hike would have caused 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields to fall sharply and signaled stronger Fed credibility, despite likely triggering a steeper equity market drop.
Import and export prices, averaging 7.8%, serve as a measure of underlying inflation without seasonal or quality adjustments, while core PCE at 3.3% is trending higher above its pre-COVID baseline.
Apparent economic strength in GDP Now models may reflect inventory accumulation driven by fear of rising prices and consumer or retailer hoarding rather than genuine underlying demand.

A severe broader stock market decline over the next few months would likely require the 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields to surge higher, catalyzed by crude oil advancing toward $140 to $150 per barrel.

AMD is projected to reach a $1 trillion-plus market cap in Q4 this year (currently just under $900 billion) as its 'ripper rally' continues, and is described as the most exciting stock on track to be a trillion-dollar company in 2027.
The speaker projects AMD will become a trillion-dollar company by 2027, driven by high growth rates, intense hype, and significant upcoming Wall Street capital inflows.

Commodity inflation is widespread outside of oil, with soybeans, corn, sugar, wheat, cocoa, oats, and copper all showing significant price increases, whereas lumber raw prices are down significantly in a manner that appears recessionary.
Broad commodity baskets like GSG are flashing warning signs, while severe market downside would require 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields to explode much higher.
